examples.text: This is the coldest winter I remember.
examples.note: Cold + est: the coldest

examples.text: Her handwriting is neater than mine.
examples.note: Neat + er: neater

examples.text: He is the fastest runner in the school.
examples.note: Fast + est: the fastest

examples.text: A mouse is smaller than a cat.
examples.note: Small + er: smaller

examples.text: This road is wideer than the old one.
examples.correction: This road is wider than the old one.
examples.note: Wide ends in e, so add only r

examples.text: She is the prettyest girl in the class.
examples.correction: She is the prettiest girl in the class.
examples.note: Pretty changes y to i: prettiest

examples.text: The new phone is thiner than the old one.
examples.correction: The new phone is thinner than the old one.
examples.note: Thin doubles the n: thinner

examples.text: This soup is the tastyest in town.
examples.correction: This soup is the tastiest in town.
examples.note: Tasty changes y to i: tastiest

examples.text: The shape was the largeest in the room.
examples.correction: The shape was the largest in the room.
examples.note: Large ends in e, so add only st

examples.text: My bag is heavyer than yours.
examples.correction: My bag is heavier than yours.
examples.note: Heavy changes y to i: heavier

examples.text: It is necessary to book a table early.
examples.note: Necessary: one c, two s

examples.text: I felt embarrassed when I forgot his name.
examples.note: Embarrassed: double r and double s

examples.text: The committee made its decision on Friday.
examples.note: Committee: double m and double t

examples.text: We stayed in cheap accommodation near the station.
examples.note: Accommodation: double c and double m

examples.text: She was embarassed by the question.
examples.correction: She was embarrassed by the question.
examples.note: Embarrassed: double r and double s

examples.text: It is neccessary to bring your passport.
examples.correction: It is necessary to bring your passport.
examples.note: Necessary: one c, two s

examples.text: I see her ocasionally at the gym.
examples.correction: I see her occasionally at the gym.
examples.note: Occasionally: double c, one s

examples.text: He disapeared after the show.
examples.note: Disappear: double p after dis-

examples.text: It is a great oportunity for us.
examples.correction: It is a great opportunity for us.
examples.note: Opportunity: double p

examples.text: The comittee meets every month.
examples.note: Committee: double m and double t
